$comment: design §10.5 and amendment N#4 (the destination manifest): every writer S11 and S12 run resolves its destination from the environment the run hands it, and that destination must be inside the root its class declares in `run.json.destinations`. This table is the writer inventory — which writer writes under which class, which environment overrides decide its path, and what each writer falls back to when an override is unset. `runlib/destinations.py` reads it; it decides nothing this table does not state. The fallback is stated here ONLY so drift is decidable: the suite reads each `fallback_source` file and fails when the literal is no longer there, which is why a copy is tolerable where a silent one would not be. The run never relies on a fallback — an unset required override is OVERRIDE_MISSING before the first effect, because a fallback is a path the run did not declare even when it happens to land inside the fixture HOME. The class belongs to the (writer, override) PAIR rather than to the writer: one environment variable has one value, so a variable two writers read must name one class for both - `AGENT_BIOS_STATE_DIR` is the private state root for install.sh, the private installer and the shell integration alike, while the shell integration's own rc-file edit goes under ZDOTDIR. A writer that takes no override declares the class it writes under directly in `writes_without_override`.

writers.$comment: The compatibility installer writes the two host config homes and the private state root. Its own STATE_DIR line is unconditional, so the override reaches it through the environment it is handed rather than through a shell default.
The private installer. It reads its whole environment through `self.env`, so the run's overrides reach it without a shell.
The shell connection record and the rc-file edit. ZDOTDIR falling back to HOME is why HOME alone is not enough to confine this writer.

The nudge baseline the launcher reads. Its fallback goes through `pathlib.Path.home()`, which reads HOME when set and the password database when not — so an unset override here can resolve to the real home of whoever runs the process. That is the sharpest case for OVERRIDE_MISSING.

One commit per applied item. The destination is the working tree the run was given, which has no environment override: the confinement is that the tree is the fixture clone named by the `checkout` class, never a worktree sharing the owner's .git.
The close writes the ledger, the version registry and the coverage state, all inside the checkout. The nudge is its own class because it is written last and by another writer.

A personal-layer patch is applied under the owner's own layer root. HOME is required with no fallback declared, because a personal layer resolved from the password database is the one case where a missing override writes outside every root the run named.
Recovery writes only its own journal and report, under the class whose root exists so that a recovery after a drifted apply has somewhere to land that the apply did not touch.
The write-ahead journal itself. It is runtime state rather than part of the run so that a run directory lost with its machine does not take the record of what was already applied with it.
